definition: to stop a planned action before it is finished because of a problem

collocations.example: The team had to abort the mission after the storm hit.
Engineers decided to abort the launch due to an engine fault.

definition: in or to a foreign country, away from your own country

collocations.example: She decided to study abroad for one year in France.
Our managers often travel abroad to meet new clients.

definition: the fact of not being present at a place or event

collocations.example: She could not explain her absence from the meeting.
In the absence of the manager, his deputy made the decision.

definition: the use of something in a wrong or harmful way

collocations.example: The report revealed a serious abuse of power by officials.
The expense system is open to abuse by staff.

definition: a school or college that teaches a special subject or skill

collocations.example: He trained for three years at the military academy.
Only top students can enter the music academy each year.

definition: responsible for your actions and expected to explain them

collocations.example: Managers must be held accountable for their team's results.
Each worker is accountable for the quality of their work.

definition: to slowly collect or gather more and more of something over time

collocations.example: He hoped to accumulate wealth through careful investment.
Young workers accumulate experience during their first few years.

definition: correct and exact, with no mistakes

collocations.example: The company must keep accurate records of all sales.
An accurate measurement is needed before we order the parts.

definition: a steady pain that is not sharp but lasts a while

collocations.example: After the long flight she felt a dull ache in her back.
He went home early with a bad stomach ache.

definition: to succeed in reaching a goal after effort

collocations.example: The team worked hard to achieve its sales goal this year.
She achieved success by planning each project carefully.

definition: to accept or admit that something is true

collocations.example: The board acknowledged the need for faster changes.
A good leader will acknowledge a mistake and fix it.

definition: to get or gain something, such as a skill or knowledge

collocations.example: New staff acquire skills quickly through our training program.
He acquired useful knowledge during his time abroad.

definition: the act of buying or taking control of another company

collocations.example: The recent acquisition added two new factories to the firm.
The acquisition cost was higher than investors expected.

definition: a unit for measuring the area of land, about 4,047 square meters

collocations.example: They bought several acres of land for the new factory.
The company owns a few acres near the harbor.

definition: a person who cannot stop using a harmful drug

collocations.example: The clinic offers help to any drug addict who wants it.
As a recovering addict, he now speaks to young people.

definition: enough in amount or good enough for a purpose

collocations.example: We cannot guarantee adequate supplies of raw materials.
Adequate preparation is the key to a good interview.

definition: to change something slightly to make it better or more correct

collocations.example: The store had to adjust the price after the sale ended.
He was forced to adjust his schedule to meet the deadline.

definition: the work of managing and running a business or organization

collocations.example: She has a master's degree in business administration.
Too much time is spent on administration instead of sales.

definition: relating to the work of managing and organizing a business

collocations.example: I spend much of my time on administrative duties.
The company is trying to lower its administrative costs.

definition: a person whose job is to manage and organize a company or office

collocations.example: The office administrator keeps all our files neat and in order.
He is well-meaning but a rather poor administrator.

definition: the money you pay to enter a place or event

collocations.example: The museum raised its admission fee last month.
The admission price is eight dollars for adults.

definition: a young person who is developing from a child into an adult

collocations.example: The counselor works with every troubled adolescent at the school.
The program helps a young adolescent build healthy habits.

definition: to start to use a new method, plan, or way of doing things

collocations.example: The company decided to adopt a new remote-work policy.
There is little incentive to adopt such costly measures.

definition: to publicly support an idea or way of doing something

collocations.example: Many experts advocate change in how we train staff.
The report strongly advocates investing more in safety.

definition: a warm feeling of liking or caring for someone

collocations.example: She still speaks about her first boss with great affection.
He finds it hard to show affection to his coworkers.

definition: to state firmly that something is true

collocations.example: The director affirmed the company's commitment to its staff.
I can affirm that no one will lose their job.

definition: a business that provides a service for other people or companies

collocations.example: She was hired by a busy advertising agency in the city.
We booked the whole trip through a travel agency.

definition: a list of things to be discussed at a meeting

collocations.example: The next item on the agenda is the budget.
Customer safety is at the top of the agenda today.

definition: behaving in an angry or forceful way that may cause harm

collocations.example: The manager warned staff that aggressive behavior is not allowed.
He becomes aggressive whenever someone questions his plan.

definition: the work of growing crops and raising animals for food

collocations.example: Modern agriculture relies heavily on new technology.
The region still depends on agriculture for most jobs.

definition: something you hope to achieve; a goal

collocations.example: The main aim of the project is to cut waste.
Teamwork is needed to achieve these aims.

definition: a vehicle that can fly, such as a plane or helicopter

collocations.example: The passenger aircraft can seat two hundred people.
Several military aircraft flew over the base this morning.

definition: a company that carries people or goods by plane

collocations.example: She works as a pilot for a major airline.
The airline ticket cost more than we expected.

definition: a book with blank pages for keeping photos or stamps

collocations.example: She stuck all the holiday pictures into a photo album.
He keeps his rare stamps in an old stamp album.

definition: watching carefully and ready to notice or act

collocations.example: Drivers must stay alert during the long night shift.
The bank is alert to the danger of online fraud.

definition: strange and very different from what you are used to

collocations.example: Such an attitude is alien to most business leaders.
At first the new office felt like an alien culture to her.

definition: to say that someone did something wrong, without proof yet

collocations.example: The customers allege that the company hid the risks.
The report alleges fraud by two senior managers.

definition: an agreement between groups to work together for a shared goal

collocations.example: The two firms formed a strategic alliance last year.
Several small airlines formed an alliance to cut costs.

definition: to give out money, time, or resources for a particular purpose

collocations.example: The board agreed to allocate funds for new equipment.
Try to allocate enough time for each task.

definition: a person or group that helps and supports another

collocations.example: He is a close ally of the company president.
The senator lost a trusted political ally today.
